'''Jānis Polis''' (25 June 1938 – 12 April 2011) was a [[Soviet people|Soviet]] and [[Latvian people|Latvian]] [[pharmacologist]] and the developer of one of the first methods of synthesis of [[rimantadine]], which was discovered in 1963 by William W. Prichard of Du Pont & Co.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.diena.lv/lat/politics/hot/miris-remantadina-izgudrotajs-janis-polis |title=Miris Remantadīna izgudrotājs Jānis Polis |publisher=[[Diena]] |work=[[LETA]] |language=Latvian |date=12 April 2011 |accessdate=13 April 2011}}<br>- [http://www.freepatentsonline.com/3352912.pdf US patent 3352912 to W. W. Prichard]<br>- [http://www.freepatentsonline.com/4551552.html United States Patent № 4551552: Process for preparing rimantadine]: ''Rimantadine and related compounds useful as antivirals were first described by Prichard in U.S. Pat. Nos. 3,352,912 and 3,592,934. Both patents describe the preparation of rimantadine from the corresponding ketone oxime by reduction with lithium aluminum hydride.''</ref> He was born in [[Eleja parish]], Latvia. On 6 February 2009, Polis was awarded the [[WIPO]] Award for Outstanding Inventors.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lrpv.lv/index.php?lang=EN&id=17&news=179 |title=WIPO Awards Presented to a Latvian Inventor and an Innovative Enterprise |publisher=Patent Office of the Republic of Latvia |date=9 February 2009 |accessdate=13 April 2011 |archive-date=22 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120322164303/http://www.lrpv.lv/index.php?lang=EN&id=17&news=179 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Polis died in [[Riga]], [[Latvia]] on 12 April 2011 at the age of 72.
